gotchas: The stock Gen 3 device speaks NOTHING on the LAN. Every value goes to Emporia's cloud and comes back over the internet. The Gen 3 gained a 10/100Base-T RJ45 LAN port (vendor spec) but it is an uplink to the same cloud, not a local API. For a cabin on intermittent Starlink this is the whole story: no internet, no data.

Emporia's own MCP README calls the implementation 'in BETA and is subject to change moving forwards'. This is vendor-published code, not a versioned protocol specification. Treat the endpoints as vendor-sourced but mutable, and re-check before building.

Two origins with two different header names for the SAME token. c-api.emporiaenergy.com wants `Authorization: <IdToken>`; api.emporiaenergy.com wants `AuthToken: <IdToken>`. The vendor client still uses the legacy origin for device discovery (GET /customers/devices) while using c-api /v1 for everything else, so a drive

Power resolution on the vendor v1 API bottoms out at MINUTES / FIFTEEN_MINUTES. The community-documented legacy /AppAPI path can ask for 1-second instant data (see the emporia-cloud-appapi dialect). `circuit_ids` is REQUIRED and must be non-empty when querying power or energy usage for any energy-monitor device type; the vendor client throws before making the request otherwise. So a driver must call /v1/customers/devices/channels first and cannot poll blind.
unmappedReports: Per-circuit power — the device measures 3 mains channels plus up to 16 branch circuits and the API returns them keyed by circuit_id. `ac-power` is single-valued per device, so 19 measurements collapse to one. This is the central shape mismatch for this device, not a missing kind., Channel/circuit identity itself — `/v1/customers/devices/channels` returns mains vs branch channels, channel_id, channel_num, parent_channel_id and merged channels. The contract has no notion of sub-channels on one device., Per-phase AC voltage — the hardware has 3 voltage-measurement channels (vendor spec); `ac-voltage` is single-valued. A split-phase 120/240 V cabin loses the leg split. (The cloud API does not expose voltage at all — see gotchas — so this bites only via the ESPHome path.), Import vs export / net metering — the retail claim is solar and net-metering monitoring, and a mains CT reads signed. There is no `grid-power` MetricKind and the sign convention is what carries the import/export meaning. Same gap already recorded for Victron GX., Energy over an arbitrary window at an arbitrary resolution — the API's natural unit is energy between `start` and `end` at MINUTES…YEARS. The contract offers only `ac-energy-today` and `ac-energy-total`; the mapping to `ac-energy-today` requires asking for DAYS resolution and is a driver convention, not something the device reports., Device state-of-charge for the Emporia home battery (/v1/devices/batteries/state-of-charge) maps cleanly to `state-of-charge`, but it belongs to a different DeviceKind (`battery`) that is not one of the models surveyed here., EV charging sessions and reports (/v1/devices/evses/sessions, /v1/customers/ev-charging-report) — no MetricKind, and arguably correct to have none.
